articles.title: Thousands rally in Czech Republic against state media funding changes
articles.excerpt: Tens of thousands of people have taken to the streets of the Czech capital to protest against proposed changes to the funding of public service media, which critics fear could weaken broadcaster indep...
articles.body_text:
Tens of thousands of people have taken to the streets of the Czech capital to protest against proposed changes to the funding of public service media, which critics fear could weaken broadcaster independence.

Many of the protesters assembled in Letna Park in Prague on Sunday afternoon.

Some of the demonstrators wore pointed hats folded out of newspapers in tribute to an animated character who has introduced Czech Television’s nightly children’s bedtime stories for decades.

Local authorities anticipated a large crowd days before the November 17 holiday commemorating the 1989 Velvet Revolution against Communist rule, which propelled dissident playwright Vaclav Havel to power.

Under the proposed changes introduced last month, the government of billionaire Prime Minister Andrej Babis wants to replace the current monthly fee of 205 crowns ($9.45), which is charged to each household, with funding from the state budget.

Opponents say the change will stifle media freedom as it will make the outlets more dependent on the state. The government insists the plan will not affect editorial independence or programme content.

The bill has passed a preliminary vote ⁠⁠in parliament and awaits further debate.

Broadcast workers have been striking against the proposal since June and earlier this month public media employees staged a one-day strike, leading to state media boycotts by artists and students.

The Million Moments for Democracy group organised Sunday’s demonstration and said “Babis and his government obviously think they will get away with anything… that they can ignore experts, silence critics and treat democratic institutions like their property”.

The group said the protest might be “the largest public gathering in Czech history”, as organisers expect 400,000 to 600,000 demonstrators.

Although trust in the media is low – about 30 percent to 33 percent according to the latest Reuters Institute Digital News Report – public service journalism is among the most trusted news sources in the country, with Czech Television the most-watched broadcaster across several age groups.

The proposed media reform has attracted international attention: the European Broadcasting Union, the European Federation of Journalists, Reporters Without Borders and the International Press Institute have all criticised it.

articles.title: Buttigieg takes swipe at Trump administration amid FAA flight chaos
articles.excerpt:
At the "What’s Next" gathering in Denver, Democratic leaders weighed the party’s future and whether they could see themselves in the 2028 presidential race.

DENVER — Former Transportation Secretary P...
articles.body_text:
At the "What’s Next" gathering in Denver, Democratic leaders weighed the party’s future and whether they could see themselves in the 2028 presidential race.

DENVER — Former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg took a swipe at the Trump administration’s handling of Friday’s nationwide FAA ground stop, joking that he would help stranded travelers rebook flights as delays and cancellations continued.

I’ll begin with a public service announcement," Buttigieg told reporters in Denver. "I will be available in the hotel bar following the concert for anybody who needs to rebook their flights or get a refund per your rights."

He made the remark as the "What’s Next" conference wrapped up in Denver. The two-day gathering, hosted by Majority Democrats, brought leaders together to discuss the party’s direction after its midterm victories.

DEMS DESCEND ON DENVER TO SIZE UP 2028; WE ASKED WHO WANTS IN THE RACE

Former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg joked he would help stranded travelers rebook flights as he weighed in on the FAA ground stop. (Paul Steinhauser/Fox News Digital)

The FAA lifted the ground stop shortly after 8 p.m. Friday, more than four hours after it began, but flights remained delayed and canceled over the weekend. The agency cited safety concerns and serious air traffic control communications issues.

Buttigieg, who said he had no inside information about the cause of the ground stop, later questioned why the aviation system’s safeguards had not prevented an outage of that scale. He said he was watching the disruption as a traveler with a flight scheduled for Saturday.

"The system has many redundancies in it, so that normally, if there’s one point of failure, something else can catch it," he said. "It is not clear to me why that redundancy did not prevent an outage of this magnitude."

SCHUMER'S LEADERSHIP RIVAL REVEALS MAJOR SENATE RULE CHANGE HE'D PURSUE IF ELECTED

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, left, and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin appear during a news conference in the James S. Brady Press Briefing Room at the White House on Nov. 13, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Shawn Thew/EPA/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Meanwhile, Trump administration officials offered a mixed account of the failure. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the cause remained under investigation, including whether a contractor made an error or equipment failed.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin later said the stoppage was not caused by artificial intelligence or a cyberattack, but by aging infrastructure that needs to be updated. President Donald Trump told Fox News that the system had broken down because of its age.

People wait in Terminal B during a nationwide ground stop at Orlando International Airport on November 13, 2026 in Orlando City. Nearly 7,000 flights have been delayed or cancelled. ( )

Friday’s disruption was the second nationwide ground stop since the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks. The first came in January 2023, when the FAA paused domestic departures for about 90 minutes because of an outage in its Notice to Air Missions system, which provides pilots with safety information.

The FAA said at the time it found no evidence of a cyberattack. Buttigieg ordered a review of that outage and directed the agency to report on what happened and recommend steps to prevent a recurrence.

Amanda Macias covers the intersection of business, economics and politics, with a focus on how policy decisions shape markets, businesses and American workers.

articles.title: Transportation secretary Sean Duffy blames prior presidents and Congress for flight stoppage
articles.excerpt:
Democratic senator Chris Van Hollen says Trump administration hasn’t properly invested existing funds

Donald Trump’s administration on Sunday blamed the travel chaos stemming from Friday’s four-hour ...
articles.body_text:
Democratic senator Chris Van Hollen says Trump administration hasn’t properly invested existing funds

Donald Trump’s administration on Sunday blamed the travel chaos stemming from Friday’s four-hour nationwide flight stoppage on prior presidents as well as a lack of congressional funding – though a Democratic senator argued that the Trump administration hasn’t properly invested all of the funds it has already been given to implement needed air travel infrastructure upgrades.

“I take responsibility for what was given to me by prior administrations,” the US transportation secretary, Sean Duffy, told CNN’s Dana Bash, a day after he said routine but necessary maintenance botched by a contractor had caused Friday’s Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop, leading to the delay or cancellation of thousands of flights.

Meanwhile, Democratic senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland criticized how the Trump administration has managed existing funding allocated for the improvements coveted by Duffy.

“It’s really rich to hear the secretary pointing the fingers at Congress when Congress has given the administration what they asked for,” Van Hollen separately told CNN’s Bash on Sunday morning. “If they need more, they should come up and justify it. I will support what is necessary to have a safe system and a reliable system.”

Duffy claimed the congressional funding which Van Hollen mentioned – $12.5bn – was limited in scope and not nearly enough.

“I have no money in that $12.5bn that I can use for a new architecture for telecom,” said Duffy. “I can’t build new software to manage our airplanes in the airspace because it dates back to the 1990s, but there’s no money for that. There’s no money for towers. Our towers are old.”

Duffy also spent part of the interview with CNN defending Trump, who waited until Sunday to remark on the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years.

The president’s comments came in the form of social media posts blaming the Biden administration and describing himself as busy “in the White House having meetings on many subjects”. They came after he had posted about what he envisioned to be a bipartisan congressional initiative to revitalize the motion picture and television industries.

“Before I even was sworn in, the president who loves the airspace was telling me we have to modernize,” Duffy said to Bash. “This is the first president we have who cares this much about modernizing the airspace.”

When asked why Trump took two days to comment on the ground stop, Duffy claimed he was in constant behind-the-scene contact with the president.

“He was fully engaged because this is important to him, and it’s important to America,” Duffy claimed. “The president is fully supportive, fully engaged, and was fully tracking what’s happening.”

In a post on Truth Social on Sunday, Trump blamed Joe Biden and demanded funding from Congress.

“The Biden Administration was an FAA disaster. Everything they touched turned bad,” Trump wrote. “We have the knowledge and plan for the Flight Control Systems, we need Congress to give the money, FAST!”

In another interview on Sunday on CBS News’ Face the Nation, Duffy told host Margaret Brennan that the FAA was currently investigating the root cause of the botched maintenance work that triggered the ground stop. He said the maintenance involved – replacing telecommunication lines from old copper wire to fiber optic cables – has occurred “thousands of times” without any issues.

The contractor, L3Harris, is reportedly conducting diagnostics testing. Duffy, as he has repeatedly done, said there continued being no indication of a foreign cyberattack. Professional Aviation Safety Specialists (Pass), the AFL-CIO labor union representing more than 11,000 workers at the FAA, said technicians it represents were not involved in the upgrades that led to the ground stop.

“The issue was isolated to two contractor owned and maintained routers that were being updated midday,” the union said in a statement. “Historically, contractors have followed a protocol where FAA employees conduct a risk assessment and coordinate the maintenance of the system or equipment.”

But the union said Pass-represented technicians were not involved in the upgrades at the center of Friday’s ground stop.

Duffy told Brennan in response to the union’s statement that “this was done appropriately, which by the way, it’s been done thousands of times by us, by others, by other companies”.

“This has never happened,” Duffy argued. “That’s why when you have a remote location like this, we felt comfortable doing it in the middle of the day because it’s been done thousands of times. We’ve never had this situation. We’re going to have to re-evaluate when we do this work.”

When asked if a risk assessment was conducted, Duffy did not directly answer. He said: “We do risk assessments on everything.”

Duffy also cited a Government Accountability Office report published in September 2026 that noted the need to modernize air traffic control systems.

He was asked about the report noting that “it could be prioritizing speed over costs and air traffic disruptions” in implementing a modernization effort of air traffic control systems. Duffy claimed, “In regard to speed, we are going, I think … at that the right speed.”

Pass has also called for progress on improving staffing of certified professional technicians at the FAA – and for the union to be fully engaged in efforts to implement what has been dubbed the Brand New Air Traffic Control System.

“These employees should receive training on new equipment and could ensure more robust installation and optimization – if the workforce were properly staffed,” the union added.

articles.title: Cruise passengers sharply divided over cutting buffet lines to sneak quick bites
articles.excerpt: Florida-based etiquette expert Jacqueline Whitmore reveals why diners should wait until everyone has finished eating before plates are removed and shares the proper silverware signal for indicating a ...
articles.body_text:
Florida-based etiquette expert Jacqueline Whitmore reveals why diners should wait until everyone has finished eating before plates are removed and shares the proper silverware signal for indicating a pause.

A common cruise ship buffet habit is raising questions — and eyebrows — about what passengers should and shouldn't do while filling their plates during meals.

Cutting ahead of others to grab just one item may seem a harmless action, but it can frustrate fellow passengers who have been patiently waiting their turn.

Buffet line-cutting was recently highlighted in a discussion about etiquette while at sea, according to the "Royal Caribbean Blog."

CRUISE BUFFET GUESTS FACE SURPRISE CHARGES FOR TAKING FOOD BACK TO CABINS

Passengers should wait their turn even if they only want something quick, such as a piece of toast or fruit, rather than squeezing past others or reaching around them, the blog advised.

Jumping ahead generally sends the wrong message, said Diane Gottsman, an etiquette expert based in Texas.

A common cruise ship buffet habit of grabbing an item out of turn is stirring a debate about etiquette while at sea.  (iStock)

"It's never acceptable to jump in front of someone in a buffet line, whether on a cruise ship, at a restaurant buffet or at a wedding," Gottsman said.

"Everyone is waiting their turn, so having someone jump in front of you comes across as rude," she added. "It also disrupts the flow of the buffet line, and in some cases can even cause a buffet traffic jam."

CRUISE PASSENGERS CRITICIZE NEW PROGRAM IDENTIFYING EARLY TIPPERS ON BOARD

There may be exceptions, however, depending on what someone needs and how crowded the buffet may be.

Gottsman said reaching in for a napkin is more understandable than cutting ahead to grab food. If only a few people are waiting, politely asking to step in briefly for a fork or knife may also be acceptable.

Holding a place for someone else can also test the patience of passengers who have been waiting.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"If you're holding a space for your spouse, a friend or a child, the child generally gets a pass," said Gottsman. But the spouse and friend are probably being judged and frustrating others who have been standing in line for 20 or 30 minutes."

Cutting ahead on a cruise ship buffet line can frustrate fellow passengers and disrupt the flow of dinner traffic, said an etiquette expert. (Corbis via Getty Images)

If another passenger does cut the line, however, Gottsman generally advises against confronting the person over a minor offense.

For someone who repeatedly jumps ahead, she suggested speaking with a manager in the dining area and allowing staff to handle the situation.

Cruise passengers themselves appear divided over exactly where to draw the line.

Experts say politely asking others in line before stepping ahead can help avoid tension among passengers at crowded buffets. (iStock)

In a Reddit discussion, a traveler asked whether it was acceptable to skip ahead when people were waiting for the first dish at a buffet, but there was no line for other items farther down.

"If there's a wide opening, it's fine. If you're squeezing in between people, then go wait in line like everyone else," one person wrote.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Another commenter said the deciding factor should be whether the move holds up anyone already waiting.

"If they have to wait for you after getting [past] the first item, then you've cut in line," the user wrote.

"No, get in the line," another user chimed in.

Fox News Digital reached out to Royal Caribbean for more information and comment.

Kelly McGreal is a member of the lifestyle team at Fox News Digital. She and the team cover travel, food and drink, health, relationships and more. She also produces the weekly American Culture Quiz and handles other special projects.

articles.title: 'General Hospital' star Cameron Mathison says ‘red flags’ drove him to demand answers before cancer diagnosis
articles.excerpt:
The "A Very Arctic Christmas" actor tells Fox News Digital he pushed for an MRI for two years before the scan saved his life and explains how cancer transformed his approach to health.

Cameron Mathis...
articles.body_text:
The "A Very Arctic Christmas" actor tells Fox News Digital he pushed for an MRI for two years before the scan saved his life and explains how cancer transformed his approach to health.

Cameron Mathison knew something was wrong — and spent two years pushing for answers before an MRI revealed he had cancer.

The "General Hospital" star told Fox News Digital the frightening experience changed how he approaches his health, including knowing when to stop pushing his body.

"I just knew something was wrong," said Mathison, who stars in Great American Media's "A Very Arctic Christmas."

'LIONESS' STAR JILL WAGNER RAISES DAUGHTERS IN TENNESSEE TOWN OF 800, WHERE HORSES AND BUGGIES STILL ROAM

Cameron Mathison told Fox News Digital he knew something was wrong with his health before an MRI revealed kidney cancer. (Christine Bartolucci/Disney via Getty Images)

Mathison was diagnosed with renal cell carcinoma, a type of kidney cancer, in 2019 after an MRI revealed a tumor.

Before his diagnosis, the actor said he had gone to extraordinary lengths to monitor his health, undergoing bloodwork, gut microbiome testing and hormone evaluations. Despite those efforts, he said, troubling results left him searching for an explanation.

"I was a guy trying to do it right, but like I was alluding to, I was very extreme," he said. "And I was doing these extreme things, and I was getting the blood tests, and … things were just off … they were like red flags."

WATCH: CAMERON MATHISON FOUGHT FOR 2 YEARS TO GET LIFE-SAVING MRI

The experience left him with a message for others facing unanswered health questions.

"One of the lessons is to be your own best advocate for your health," he said.

BUSY PHILIPPS DIAGNOSED WITH RARE BRAIN TUMOR AFTER UNDERGOING BODY SCAN HER DOCTOR TOLD HER SHE DIDN'T 'NEED'

Surviving cancer also prompted Mathison to rethink his approach to fitness. After years of pushing himself, he said he now recognizes the importance of rest and recovery.

The "General Hospital" star recalled troubling "red flags" despite his commitment to an extensive health and wellness routine. (Cameron Mathison / Instagram)

But his cancer battle was only part of a painful series of losses.

Mathison also faced his mother's death, the end of his 22-year marriage and the loss of his family home in a wildfire. He also lost his hosting job when Hallmark Channel's "Home & Family" was canceled.

'BAYWATCH' STAR NICOLE EGGERT EXPOSES FINANCIAL TOLL OF CANCER BATTLE: 'THE BILLS DON'T STOP'

"In fact, at the time, going through a divorce which was very heartbreaking for me, I had just lost my mom, I had been through my cancer journey, I had all this loss, lost my job, and I was hanging onto that house," he said.

As the losses mounted and his children left for college, Mathison found himself confronting a difficult question about his future.

Cameron Mathison lies in a hospital bed surrounded by his two children. (Cameron Mathison / Instagram)

"And it was like, ‘Now who do you want to be?’"

The actor said those experiences challenged the assumption that making the right choices guarantees decades ahead. Instead, he has found motivation in recognizing how quickly circumstances can change.

"You know, I may not make it home. Like, it sounds depressing, but it's not. It's actually very encouraging and very motivating because you don't know how short life is going to be and to make it meaningful and be kind and loving and compassionate and wise and grateful in every moment is going to make the most of it," he said.

WATCH: CAMERON MATHISON DISHES ON CO-STAR JILL WAGNER'S WILD PRANKSTER SIDE

That appreciation for family helped draw Mathison to "A Very Arctic Christmas," which reunites him with "Lioness" star Jill Wagner.

Mathison plays Jim, a single father and former Major League Baseball player turned broadcaster, whose Arctic cruise with his 20-year-old daughter, Isla, takes an unexpected turn.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

A scheduling mix-up leaves the pair stranded after their ship departs without them. They turn to wildlife conservationist Jane, played by Wagner, to help them navigate the frozen wilderness. Maya Rose Skabar plays Isla.

Cameron Mathison said his relationship with his children helped inspire his latest holiday movie, "A Very Arctic Christmas." (Great American Media)

Mathison said the script struck a personal chord because it was inspired in part by his relationship with his children, their travels and the challenges their family has faced in recent years.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"There's a lot of humor in it, there's super, super touching moments in it. There's romance, as we love in a Christmas movie," he said.

Jill Wagner and Cameron Mathison star in "A Very Arctic Christmas," available to stream on Great American Pure Flix. (Great American Media)

He also praised Wagner's sense of humor behind the scenes.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Jill Wagner stars as Bobby in "Lioness." (Credit: Lauren "Lo" Smith/Paramount+)

"Jill is such a, sort of like a legend these days, and they see her as this sweet actress in a Christmas movie and then as a hardcore, I want to use a different word, but in ‘Lioness,’ Mathison said. "And … I don't think in any of those roles you get to see her unbelievable sense of humor. She's outrageous and so funny and is the queen of all pranks … She's just so funny, so upbeat, so positive, energizer bunny and obviously just a wealth of talent."

"A Very Arctic Christmas" is available to stream on Great American Pure Flix.

Stephanie Giang-Paunon is an entertainment reporter for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan, Egypt condemn Iranian attack on Bahrain - as it happened
articles.excerpt:
Iran has targeted airbase in Bahrain in latest resumption of strikes since september

The state-run Bahrain news agency is also carrying the statements of each country in the region responding to Iran...
articles.body_text:
Iran has targeted airbase in Bahrain in latest resumption of strikes since september

The state-run Bahrain news agency is also carrying the statements of each country in the region responding to Iran’s actions targeting their Gulf neighbour this morning.

Jordan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar have all strongly condemned the attack and expressed solidarity with Bahrain.

The statements are very similar, I’ve pulled out a few below:

Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a statement published by the Saudi Press Agency:

double quotation markThe Kingdom affirms that the Iranian attacks constitute a violation of international law and the principles of good neighborliness. The Kingdom stresses the importance of an immediate halt to the blatant Iranian attacks on the countries of the region, and of taking serious steps towards achieving security and stability for the countries of the region and their peoples.

Qatar’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a statement on the Qatar news agency (QNA):

double quotation markThe continuation of these attacks represents a dangerous escalation that will complicate efforts to contain the tension and undermine political and diplomatic endeavors aimed at achieving security and stability in the region.

I’m going to wrap up coverage for now. Here’s a summary of what you need to know as Iran steps up strikes against US allies in the Gulf again.

Iran launched a six-drone attack on a US airbase in Bahrain early on Sunday, prompting fears of a return to full-blown fighting after a two-month lull in strikes

Bahrain said it had intercepted “several aerial attacks” and destroyed the drones before they reached their targets, and officials did not immediately disclose any damage or injuries

However the tiny Gulf kingdom, which hosts a major US naval command, was forced to send out public warnings and sound missile warning sirens ahead of the incoming strikes

Residents were rattled by the attacks starting up again; the second since Friday. “I was hoping this period was behind us and wouldn’t happen again”

Iran said it had targeted a radar facility at the Al-Rifaa helicopter base. The US is yet to respond, but said there had been no damage from the first attempted strike on Friday.

Iran said its attack was justified retaliation for recent US aggression. The US has been carrying out low-level strikes on Iranian naval sites along the country’s south coast and also on Qeshm Island, in the Strait of Hormuz, to support oil vessels traversing the dangerous waterway

Iran says ships traversing the chokepoint without permission are hitting sea mines and sinking, and are legitimate targets to be fired upon.

On a different front, in civil war-torn Yemen, the Iran-backed Houthis are putting pressure on the government’s control around Aden, the interim capital.

The Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces say they’ve been forced to withdraw from their Bab el-Mandeb counter-offensive to focus on securing Aden.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards have claimed the sinking of an oil supertanker which hit a mine in the Strait of Hormuz. There’s no independent verification of this yet.

The US military had claimed recently that it had cleared all mines from the main routes through the waterway.

But the IRGC said Sunday that two ships had hit its mines while travelling through the strait, “resulting in massive explosions and fire”.

It said the super tanker had been carrying more than two million barrels of oil when it sunk in the Gulf. Iran has made several announcements in recent weeks about ships hitting mines.

Tehran has heavily restricted shipping traffic through the strait since the start of the war, demanding vessels seek permission and travel via designated pathways. It has fired on ships trying to circumvent Iranian detection.

The US has been supporting ships going through the strait. In the past 24 hours, Centcomm posted on X a picture of F-16 fighter jets and said that more than 1.7 billions of crude oil “have been shipped through the Strait of Hormuz by Gulf partners with U.S. protection.”

As I mentioned earlier, Iran’s Revolutionary Guards have said its strikes this morning were retaliation for US aggression.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said at a press conference in Tehran on Sunday that Iran would continue to respond to any military aggression by the US or other states.

He was asked whether the strike on Tehran, the second this weekend, showed a change in Iranian direction as negotiations with the US have stalled.

Mr. Baghaei said that Iran was “not waiting for anyone” and was focused on its security.

The US has launched strikes on Iranian naval bases in the Strait of Hormuz in recent weeks, as well as along Iran’s southern coast. This has been seen as efforts to try and degrade Iran’s striking capability as well as offering cover for commerical ships still venturing through and out of Hormuz.

President Trump has refrained from major military escalation, describing those sporadic strikes as minor. However, American media have reported that both the US and Israel have discussed plans for a fuller resumption of strikes.

Here’s a map showing Bahrain, the smallest Gulf state, in relation to Iran and the rest of its Gulf neighbours. Tehran sent a flurry of drones across the Gulf in the early hours of Sunday morning to target a US air base south of Manama.

Bahrain is home to a major US military base, the NSA Bahrain (or Naval Support Activity Bahrain), which are headquarters for the US Fifth Fleet and US Naval Forces Central Command, and also acts as key hub of support for all operations in the region.

However the base was struck heavily during Iran’s retaliatory strikes at the start of the war, and it’s unclear whether it’s fully recovered.

American media have reported major damage to its headquarters, barracks and radar facilities.

Iran’s drones this morning were aimed at a different target- the US air base in Al-Rifaa, south of the capital.

The US has formal bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, and Qatar, and access arrangements to military facilities in the United Arab Emirates, Oman, and Saudi Arabia.

In light of Iran’s latest strike attempts on US allies in the Gulf, it’s useful to look at what the US commander-in-chief has been saying in recent days, as my colleague Patrick Wintour reports.
 
 
 Donald Trump has said in a series of media interviews since Thursday that he will attack Iran only if necessary, claiming that Gulf countries, such as Saudi Arabia, have urged him to hold back from planned large-scale military strikes.

Trump said he had asked the vice-president, JD Vance, to end his interest in negotiating a new deal with Iran and instead focus on corruption and fraud in Democrat-run cities and states.

Vance had been seen by the Iranians as the most trustworthy figure close to Trump, but they had rejected his request for a personal meeting with their negotiators to discuss the terms of a peace deal.

Vance has been at the forefront of Republicans saying the war was the cause of the widespread Republican losses in the midterms. Trump said he had been disappointed in the American public because higher diesel prices were a small price to pay for preventing Iran from acquiring a nuclear weapon.

I reported earlier that Yemeni government forces are falling back to Aden to try and secure their interim capital which is coming under pressure from Houthi forces.

A Houthi attack on a checkpoint near Aden has killed five people and injured eight others near Aden, AFP is reporting.

The missile targeted a checkpoint in Khor Omeira, Lahj province, AFP says, citing three unnamed military sources and a government source.

The state-run Bahrain news agency is also carrying the statements of each country in the region responding to Iran’s actions targeting their Gulf neighbour this morning.

Jordan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar have all strongly condemned the attack and expressed solidarity with Bahrain.

The statements are very similar, I’ve pulled out a few below:

Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a statement published by the Saudi Press Agency:

double quotation markThe Kingdom affirms that the Iranian attacks constitute a violation of international law and the principles of good neighborliness. The Kingdom stresses the importance of an immediate halt to the blatant Iranian attacks on the countries of the region, and of taking serious steps towards achieving security and stability for the countries of the region and their peoples.

Qatar’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a statement on the Qatar news agency (QNA):

double quotation markThe continuation of these attacks represents a dangerous escalation that will complicate efforts to contain the tension and undermine political and diplomatic endeavors aimed at achieving security and stability in the region.

Below is the full statement from Bahrain’s foreign ministry on the Iranian drone strikes today, which were intercepted and shot down. This has been published in Bahrain’s various state-controlled media outlets.

double quotation markThe Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed the Kingdom of Bahrain’s strongest condemnation of the continued Iranian aggression against its territory, including the attack launched today, Sunday, November 15, 2026, by drones that were intercepted and destroyed by air defense systems in the Kingdom’s airspace.

This comes two days after a similar attack at dawn on Friday, November 13, 2026, by two drones that were also intercepted. The Iranian Revolutionary Guard explicitly claimed responsibility for these attacks. The Ministry praised the efficiency, vigilance, and capability of the Bahrain Defense Force in confronting today’s attack and its complete readiness to deter any aggression.
  
  The Ministry considered these attacks a resumption of Iran’s heinous aggression against the Kingdom and countries in the region, disregarding the provisions of international law and the principles of the UN Charter.

The Kingdom views them as a blatant attack on its sovereignty and territorial integrity, a flagrant violation of Security Council Resolution 2817, which condemned Iranian attacks on the Kingdom of Bahrain and neighboring countries and demanded their immediate cessation, a targeting of innocent citizens and residents, a sabotage of de-escalation efforts, and a serious threat to the region’s security and stability.
  
  The Ministry affirmed the Kingdom of Bahrain’s categorical rejection of the flimsy pretexts and baseless claims put forward by the Iranian Revolutionary Guard, emphasizing that no pretext justifies aggression against the sovereignty and territorial integrity of states.

It stressed that freedom of navigation and passage, by sea and air, in straits used for international navigation is a right guaranteed by the rules of international law and is not subject to the will or conditions of any state.

The Kingdom also rejects the transformation of its territory into an arena for settling scores and holds Iran fully responsible for these attacks and their consequences.
  
  The Ministry also affirmed the Kingdom of Bahrain’s inherent right, both individually and collectively, to self-defense in accordance with Article (51) of the Charter, and to take all necessary measures to safeguard its sovereignty and the security of its citizens and residents, in close coordination with its brothers in the Gulf Cooperation Council, based on the Joint Defense Agreement, which considers an attack on any member state an attack on all, as well as with its allies and partners. The Ministry noted that the Kingdom of Bahrain, as a member of the UN Security Council, calls upon the Council to condemn these repeated attacks and demands that it assume its responsibilities and take decisive measures to ensure Iran’s full compliance with Resolution 2817, and to halt its attacks, threats, and support for proxy groups in the region. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs added that the Kingdom of Bahrain affirms that its security is a red line, that its sovereignty is non-negotiable, and that it will remain, as it has always been, a proponent of good neighborliness, respect for the sovereignty of states, and non-interference in their affairs, and is committed to the security and stability of the Arabian Gulf.

Iranian media are reporting that their foreign minister Abbas Araqchi will be in Oman on Tuesday for talks with his Omani counterpart.

Oman, along with Qatar, has been one of the key negotiators in ceasefire and peace talks between Tehran and Washington.

As both sides have settled into a strategy of exerting continued economic pain on the other, we’re yet to see any movement on a deal though.

The US is maintaining a highly expensive military operation in the Gulf, with a naval blockade that aims to stop Iranian oil ships leaving the Persian Gulf, thereby hurting the Iranian economy, and through a missile and drone operation targeting Iran’s southern coastline aimed at protecting and helping commercial ships get out. Oil flows are said to be back near their prewar level.

But Iran hasn’t strayed from its demands, and the conditions it wants to end the war: a measure of control over Hormuz, removal of the blockade and economic sanctions, having its assets unfrozen, and reparations.

I mentioned earlier the withdrawal of Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces from the areas around Bab el-Mandeb where they’ve been attempting to stave off the Houthis.

A lightning-strike offensive back in September saw the Houthis sweep almost the entire Red Sea coast and almost seize control of the critical Red Sea strait, which has become another chokepoint in the flow of oil and and energy supplies from Gulf producers.

Here’s the full statement from the Yemeni forces, who are now redeploying towards Aden, where their government is based.

The Houthis are gathering steam in the south, where most areas remain under government control.

double quotation markThe Southern Armed Forces announce the implementation of a redeployment ‌operation for its forces from Dhubab Airport and the Bab el-Mandeb area, west of Taiz Governorate.

This step is taken based on the priority of securing the capital, Aden, and the neighbouring governorates, as well as strengthening the front lines and addressing existing threats.

The Houthis’ stronghold currently remains most of northern Yemen, where they control the capital Sanaa and other populous areas. Since the civil war erupted in 2014, the Houthis have pushed the internationally-recognised Yemeni government south and stunned the Saudi-backed administration with their push south in September.

That prompted a military fight back operation, and Saudi Arabia striking Houthi areas in Yemen as the Houthis targeted airports and oil supplies in the Gulf kingdom.

The US thinks Iran still has between 1,500-2,500 missiles in its arsenal despite the US-Israeli damage done this year to its production facilities, reports the Wall St Journal.

That’s the “low confidence” assessment from intelligence analysts, the American paper reports, citing US officials.

They noted difficulties with tracking Iran’s stockpile, and assessing whether they’re ready for launch or remain in storage.

But they noted that Iran has appeared to manage to slowly rebuild its arsenal during the long lulls in fighting and mostly from stockpiled weapons components. Tehran has also kept up a ready supply of drones and short-range missiles.

The assessment would go against what Trump and his Secretary of Defence/War, Peter Hegseth, have been claiming repeatedly throughout the nearly-nine months of war so far; that the US has “decimated” Iran’s long-range fighting capability.

Both the US and Israel had also stated the goal of destroying Iran’s ballistic-missile capabilities when they launched war on 28 February.

Hamas has confirmed the killing of Samir Mahmoud Hassan Abu Younis, commander of the group’s Rafah Brigade, in an Israeli airstrike on a Gaza refugee camp on Saturday night.

The BBC reports that eyewitnesses in Gaza saw four missiles strike a tent in the Al-Waha camp in Al-Mawasi, which shelters hundreds of displaced people in the southern part of the strip.

The Israeli military said it had taken steps to “mitigate harm to civilians” in the strike. It said it had also targeted other Hamas militants in the strike but gave no further detail.

Israel’s military first announced the killing on Sunday, saying they had targeted Younis who they said had been working on restoring Hamas and getting members to “advance and carry out terror attacks”.

Younis had been one of the senior Hamas figures who helped plan and oversee the October 7 attacks. He had only been the Rafah brigade leader role for two months, after Israel killed his predecessor, Nael Abu Obeid.

In their statement announcing his death, Hamas said Younis was “one of the most important commanders involved in planning and overseeing the 7 October attack”.

Earlier this week, an Israeli strike on Nasser Hospital, the largest operational hospital in southern Gaza, killed at least six people, including a surgeon and patients, and injured 30, local officials said. The IDF said it had been targeting a commander of Hamas’s armed wing.

Israel is still striking Gaza on a near daily basis despite the the US-brokered ceasefire having come into action since October last year. More than 1,620 people have been killed in Gaza since the ceasefire, and more than 74,650 people have been killed in Gaza since the war began.

Here’s a recap of what the various sides have said this morning regarding the latest Iranian strikes targeting a US air base in Bahrain.

double quotation markThe US air defence radar system at the Al-Riffa helicopter base in Bahrain was targeted by six drones belonging to the IRGC Aerospace Force.

The Strait of Hormuz is closed, and any aggression by the American enemy will be met with an even harsher and more forceful response.

double quotation markIran continues its systematic hostile approach through its sinful attacks targeting the Kingdom of Bahrain.
  
  
  [Bahrain] rejects turning its territory into an arena for settling scores and holds Iran fully responsible for these attacks.

I’m yet to see a response from the US, but can expect Centcomm (which oversees all American military operations in the Middle East) to comment at some stage, like it did for Friday’s attack. Those strikes also targeted a radar site.

After two months of calm, the explosions have started again for Bahrain citizens.

Locals reported hearing blasts about 4am local time, and then a second round at 6.30am.

double quotation markIt’s exactly what I was hoping wouldn’t happen: Iranian attacks starting again, with all the worry and uncertainty that go with them”, Hayat Ibrahim, 65, told AFP news agency.

Another resident, Mohammed Abdallah, a shopkeeper in the capital Manama, which is just north of the air base targeted said:

double quotation markI was hoping this period was behind us and wouldn’t happen again.

Bahrain’s Interior Ministry posted public warnings on X, telling “residents to remain calm, proceed to the nearest safe location, and follow news through official channels”.

Iran had last launched strikes in the first week of September, when the regime targeted US military assets in Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they had launched six drones targeting a US air defence radar at the Al-Rifaa helicopter base on Sunday morning, reported Iranian media.

They said they had attacked the air base in retaliation for “hostile US actions”. The base is about a 30-minute drive south of Manama.

US forces have been quietly carrying out a series of strikes on Iranian sites in recent weeks, including on the key Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, where there’s a major IRGC presence. Trump has called them minor strikes.
 
 
 Bahrain officials this morning have accused Tehran of continuing a “systematic hostile approach” to the kingdom.

The drone flurry this morning comes just 48 hours after Iran launched drones on Friday, the first escalations targeting Bahrain in two months.

That attack targeted an American radar facility. US Central Command said it had shot down the two drones without any injury or damage.

Bahrain officials hadn’t issued any warnings for that attack, but were forced to send out public alerts this morning telling residents to seek shelter. The Interior Ministry told locals to remain calm but proceed to to the nearest safe location.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the fighting in the Middle East.

Iran has targeted an airbase in Bahrain in the latest resumption of strikes since September, prompting public warnings and sirens to ring out in the Gulf kingdom this morning.

According to Iranian media, the IRGC said it had sent six drones to attack a US radar system hosted in the US-allied island state.

Explosions were heard around the capital, Manama, but Bahrain authorities say their air defences intercepted the attacks before they reached their targets.

Bahrain, which lies directly across the Persian Gulf from Iran, is home to the US Navy’s Fifth Fleet, and has been repeatedly attacked by Tehran during the course of the war, which has seen flare-ups in strikes amid long bouts of inaction.

There are fears Iran’s attacks this morning might signal a resumption of the war while US President Donald Trump has threatened but refrained from returning to major combat. Negotiations to end the war remain at a stalemate, with the US maintaining its naval blockade and Iran its stranglehold over the strait of Hormuz.

Developments in the Red Sea this morning will add to further concerns for Gulf oil flows.

The Yemeni government forces supported by Saudi Arabia, fighting the Houthis, have retreated from the Bab el-Mandeb area, giving the Iran-aligned rebels even greater control over the critical shipping lane, which Saudi Arabia and other Gulf oil producers had been relying on to get their supplies out.

Elsewhere, Hamas has confirmed that a senior commander involved in planning the 7 October attacks was killed in an Israeli airstrike on Saturday.

articles.title: America's first Muslim senator exposes a political blind spot
articles.excerpt:
Michigan voter Carey Bloom argues Abdul El-Sayed is ‘extremely dangerous’ not just to the Jewish community, but to ‘all of America.’

As a Muslim woman, physician and longtime critic of Islamism, I ha...
articles.body_text:
Michigan voter Carey Bloom argues Abdul El-Sayed is ‘extremely dangerous’ not just to the Jewish community, but to ‘all of America.’

As a Muslim woman, physician and longtime critic of Islamism, I have witnessed firsthand the consequences of extremist interpretations of my faith.

I have examined the bodies of Jews murdered by Hamas during the Oct. 7, 2023, terrorist attacks in Israel; recorded the testimony of Yazidi and Kurdish victims of ISIS atrocities in Iraq; interviewed children inducted into ISIS and the Taliban; consoled Christians persecuted in Iraq and Pakistan; and walked through the now-dismantled Al Hol detention camp in Syria.

I know deeply the tragedies promulgated by practitioners of my faith who believe in an extremist interpretation of the religion called Islamism or political Islam. I also know there is a rising tide of people who don’t differentiate between the two and believe all Islam is extremist.

Abdul El-Sayed holds a news conference after winning the Democratic Senate nomination in Michigan, on August 5, 2026, in Detroit, Michigan (Rich Edson/Fox News)

'POD SAVE AMERICA' HOSTS WARN EL-SAYED TO TONE DOWN 'CONDESCENSION' ON MUSLIM BROTHERHOOD QUESTIONS

Islamism and anti-Muslim bigotry took center stage in the midterm elections, which delivered the nation’s first Muslim senator-elect, Abdul El-Sayed, D-Mich.

Yet both political parties are challenged in meeting this moment. Republicans too often fail to distinguish Muslims from Islamists, while Democrats seem unwilling to examine the distinction at all. Accusations of "Islamophobia," amplified by the politics of identity and "anti-racism," have further obscured a debate Americans urgently need to have.

Too often, Islamophobia is conflated with anti-Muslim xenophobia to the detriment of Muslim critics of Islamism who seek to expose Islamist influence and to the benefit of Islamist ideology and its allies.

Expect accusations of Islamophobia to be increasingly deployed as a means of diverting scrutiny away from El-Sayed, whose senatorial bid exposed these tensions.

During a television interview, El-Sayed denied that his family was connected to the Muslim Brotherhood. After the election, he joked about the allegations, mocking his critics.

ABDUL EL-SAYED GROWS AGITATED WITH REPORTER AFTER BEING PRESSED ON FAMILY'S ALLEGED MUSLIM BROTHERHOOD TIES

Republicans frequently mishandled the issue.

Vice President JD Vance called El-Sayed "very, very evil." President Donald Trump repeatedly labeled him a "jihadist." Rep. Nancy Mace, R-S.C., made sweeping statements questioning Muslims’ fitness for political office. Such attacks risk alienating Muslim voters and undermining legitimate scrutiny of El-Sayed’s political associations, statements and policy positions.

Republicans will continue to struggle with these questions until they understand how Islamism covertly exploits democratic institutions and electoral politics — a challenge identified overseas.

A 2025 French government report on the Muslim Brotherhood examined "Islamist entryism," or Muslim Brotherhood efforts to build influence through local institutions, associations and political structures.

EL-SAYED'S PAST MUSLIM BROTHERHOOD COMMENTS RAISE RED FLAGS AS HE EYES POWERFUL ROLE

Republicans are not alone in their failure to distinguish Islamist political activity from apolitical pluralism.

Too often, Democratic leaders dismiss legitimate questions about Islamist ideology as "Islamophobia," even as disputes over antisemitism, anti-Zionism and the Israel-Hamas conflict deepen divisions within their party.

Following the midterms, former Chicago Mayor Rahm Emanuel faced questions from Fox News host Brian Kilmeade about rising antisemitism and anti-Israel activism within Democratic politics. His responses illustrated the difficulty party leaders face in confronting these divisions.

‘DESTROYING THE AMERICAN WAY OF LIFE’: EL-SAYED’S POLITICAL ORBIT COMPLICATES EFFORT TO MODERATE HIS IMAGE

Abdul El-Sayed arrives for an event at the Arab America Foundation on Nov. 6, 2026. (Asra Q. Nomani)

Fox News Digital investigative reporter Asra Nomani documented another revealing moment three days after the election, when El-Sayed attended the Arab America Foundation’s national summit where an event leader celebrated El-Sayed’s victory with the declaration, "You destroyed AIPAC twice," before invoking "Free Palestine" and "From the river to the sea."

El-Sayed smiled as these remarks were delivered, without publicly challenging them at that moment.

The phrase "From the river to the sea" is interpreted by many Israelis and Jews as a call for Israel’s elimination, although some Palestinian advocates claim it is a demand for freedom and equal rights.

Such ambiguity makes it all the more important for elected officials to explain what these slogans mean and whether they support Israel’s continued existence as a Jewish state.

JEWISH LEADERS IN MICHIGAN PREPARE TO WORK WITH ABDUL EL-SAYED DESPITE LINGERING CONCERNS

As an expert on Islamism, I can see how such public celebration raises serious questions about the ideological expectations some supporters already place on El-Sayed. He should answer those questions directly.

The same scrutiny should extend to elected officials’ positions on antisemitism, anti-Zionism and American foreign policy toward Israel, Qatar, Turkey and Iran, countries whose relationships with Islamist movements differ substantially but remain important to U.S. national security.

Consider Rep.-elect Adam Hamawy, D-N.J., who faced questions during a CNN interview about whether he considered Iran an American adversary. His response deserves examination on its merits, particularly considering reporting about his past statements and associations.

But such scrutiny must be grounded in verifiable evidence, not assumptions based on a politician’s Muslim identity. That distinction is essential.

When all Muslims are portrayed as Islamists, genuine ideological concerns become harder to investigate. When every criticism of political Islam is dismissed as "Islamophobia," the public loses another opportunity for honest debate.

Hasan Piker, left, listens as Abdul El-Sayed speaks in a green room before a campaign rally, Tuesday, April 7, 2026, at the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor, Mich. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo)

El-Sayed’s campaign offers further examples.

He appeared alongside far-left commentator Hasan Piker, who previously said America "deserved 9/11," a remark Piker later characterized as inappropriate. Piker has also faced criticism over his commentary about Hamas and the Oct. 7 attacks. El-Sayed subsequently distanced himself from Piker.

Politicians shouldn't be held responsible for every statement made by their supporters. But they must be willing to reject extremist rhetoric clearly and consistently, particularly when it comes from influential figures within their own coalitions.

El-Sayed also faced criticism over his "hurt people hurt people" remarks following an attack on Temple Israel synagogue in Michigan that federal authorities investigated as a Hezbollah-inspired act of terrorism — remarks he claims were misconstrued.

Yet political leaders have a responsibility to condemn antisemitic violence unequivocally, without language that could reasonably be interpreted as legitimizing it.

Undated file picture of Hassan al-Banna, founder of the Egyptian Muslim Brotherhood in the city of Ismailya in 1929. (AFP via Getty Images)

Questions about El-Sayed’s family background and historical associations with Islamist organizations also surfaced during the campaign — allegations involving charities associated with his mother and archived social media statements attributed to his half-sister concerning the Muslim Brotherhood. El-Sayed rejects any claims that he or his family are Muslim Brotherhood affiliates.

More directly relevant are El-Sayed’s published political views. Eitan Fischberger highlighted pro-Islamist 2012 columns co-authored by El-Sayed following Islamist Mohamed Morsi’s election — Egypt’s first democratically elected president, who was ousted in 2013 amid mass protests against his government.

El-Sayed had urged recognition of the Brotherhood’s participation in Egypt’s political uprising.

Those writings are legitimate subjects for scrutiny. Americans deserve to know whether El-Sayed’s views of the Brotherhood have since changed.

Democratic Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed denied to NBC's Kristen Welker that his family had any ties to the Muslim Brotherhood. (Matthew LaVere/NBC via Getty Images)

MICHIGAN SENATE RIVALS CLASH OVER MUSLIM BROTHERHOOD ALLEGATIONS AS ROGERS DOUBLES DOWN ON EL-SAYED

We must distinguish Muslims who support liberal democracy and religious pluralism from those who seek to impose Islamist political principles.

We must also distinguish anti-Muslim hatred, discrimination and violence from legitimate criticism of religiously inspired political movements. The two are not interchangeable.

When politicians conflate them, they create a climate in which ideological scrutiny becomes more difficult and religious prejudice becomes easier to excuse.

Rejecting Islamism isn’t an act of anti-Muslim hatred. For pluralist, anti-Islamist Muslims, it is an affirmation of religious liberty, democratic government, individual rights and the separation of religious authority from state power.

A healthy, liberal democracy must protect the right of Muslims to worship, participate in politics and hold public office while also protecting the right of Americans to scrutinize any political ideology, including Islamism.

El-Sayed should be challenged vigorously on his views of the Muslim Brotherhood, Islamist political movements, antisemitism and Israel’s right to exist. His public appearances, past writings and political alliances provide legitimate starting points for that examination.

Americans must not empower politicians who excuse terrorism, defend antisemitic violence or seek to undermine constitutional democracy, regardless of their religion or political party.

Both parties should support candidates, including Muslim candidates, who defend democratic pluralism and reject political extremism.

The answer to Islamist entryism is neither anti-Muslim prejudice nor silence in the face of extremism. It is informed scrutiny, intellectual honesty and an unwavering commitment to America’s constitutional principles.

Qanta A. Ahmed, MD, is a physician, author, life member of the Council on Foreign Relations and senior fellow at Independent Women’s Forum.

articles.title: NYC DSA urges AOC to run for president while planning to take over City Council
articles.excerpt: Fox News national correspondent Bryan Llenas reports on the New York City Democratic Socialists of America's plans to gain control of the City Council, its efforts to expand its political influence ac...
articles.body_text:
Fox News national correspondent Bryan Llenas reports on the New York City Democratic Socialists of America's plans to gain control of the City Council, its efforts to expand its political influence across the city and its push for Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez to run for president in 2028 on 'Varney & Co.'

The New York City chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America overwhelmingly voted to urge Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., to run for president in 2028 on Saturday.

NYC-DSA approved a resolution making the call in a 291 to 123 vote at the chapter's annual convention. Gustavo Gordillo, co-chair of the local DSA chapter, said the vote was not a formal endorsement, but is instead a "a commitment to encouraging and building the foundation for a presidential campaign."

"AOC and New York City DSA are committed to building a stronger democratic socialist movement and DSA will create the conditions for a presidential campaign capable of advancing a working-class political agenda," Gordillo said at a press conference on Saturday.

DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS OF AMERICA LEADER SAYS ‘MANY’ IN GROUP WOULD BE 'THRILLED' AT AOC IN 2028

Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., speaks on stage during a campaign rally for New York City mayoral candidate Zohran Mamdani at Forest Hills Stadium in the Queens borough of New York City on Oct. 26, 2025. (Photo by ANGELA WEISS / AFP) (Photo by ANGELA WEISS/AFP via Getty Images)

The chapter also laid out its plans to take over New York City's City Council, among other resolutions. Several of the party's resolutions ran into controversy for appearing to be AI-generated, according to a report from Politico.

When run through the AI detection tool Pangram, the 2029 City Council election resolution was rated 100% AI-generated, the outlet reported.

Two other DSA resolutions were reportedly flagged as AI-generated as well, related to expanding DSA membership in community boards and interaction with South Asian communities.

The chapter has a policy against AI usage and voted on Saturday to formally oppose the expansion of AI.

NYC-DSA co-chair Grace Mausser pushed back on the accuracy of the Pangram results in a statement to Politico.

New York City Democratic Socialists hold a rally in Union Square on Nov. 16, 2025, to mark the start of a campaign to tax the rich and win universal childcare. (Selcuk Acar/Anadolu)

AOC CAMPAIGN MEMO FRAMES GROWTH FROM PROGRESSIVE FIREBRAND TO NATIONAL DEMOCRATIC PARTY FORCE

"We are highly skeptical of the results coming out of Pangram as resolutions are often authored and edited in consensus by multiple members," she said, adding that Pangram’s tools "are made by the same industry that’s scraped writers’ work without permission and now sells software to accuse people of not writing their own words," Mausser said.

Members of the Democratic Socialists of America gather outside of a Trump owned building during a May Day rally in New York City in 2019. (Spencer Platt/Getty Images)

Pangram claims that its service can correctly identify AI-generated text 9,999 out of 10,000 times. A University of Chicago study also found that Pangram has a near-zero error rate.

Anders Hagstrom is a reporter with Fox News Digital covering national politics and major breaking news events.

articles.excerpt:
The football world was shocked to learn former New York Jets head coach Rex Ryan was arrested after he allegedly ran over two people feet. Carton gives his take on the situation.

Rex Ryan was back on...
articles.body_text:
The football world was shocked to learn former New York Jets head coach Rex Ryan was arrested after he allegedly ran over two people feet. Carton gives his take on the situation.

Rex Ryan was back on ESPN's "Sunday NFL Countdown" show ahead of the league's Week 10 games, days after being arrested on six charges stemming from an alleged hit-and-run driving incident in Nashville.

Ryan was at his usual post discussing football and ripping people, but he did not address the incident or his arrest.

ESPN declined to explain why the former New York Jets and Buffalo Bills head coach was allowed to appear days after his arrest.

TONY ROMO HIT WITH SEVERAL NEW CITATIONS AFTER OWI ARREST, FURTHER JEOPARDIZING RETURN TO NFL BROADCASTS

This booking photo released by the Metro Nashville Police Department, shows former NFL football coach Rex Ryan.  (Metro Nashville Police Department via AP)

But a network source told OutKick that the network made its determination "based on a number of factors, which certainly includes information we have been able to gather and the conversations we have had since we became aware of the incident. We aren’t making it blindly."

That said, the source said, "with it being an active situation, there is always a chance new information is available that would cause us to reconsider our decision."

Ryan allegedly ran over Michael Holland and his wife just before midnight on Nov. 5 as they were crossing a busy roadway on the Music City’s famed Broadway street.

New York Jets head coach Rex Ryan greets quarterback Tim Tebow (15) on the sidelines during the 1st half against the Seattle Seahawks at CenturyLink Field. (Steven Bisig-USA TODAY Sports)

Holland later told the California Post that Ryan "almost killed " him and his wife with his pickup truck, as they crossed the street.

"If we had been six inches further out," Holland said, "I’d be in a hospital right now and so would my wife."

Added Holland regarding Ryan: "He decided he wanted to turn and didn’t care, and just ran over both of my feet, my wife’s foot and got her leg too."

Holland claimed Ryan ran over his feet. He took pictures of the purported injuries caused by the incident. Holland told the newspaper that Ryan didn’t stop after the incident, but he and is wife were able to catch up with him a few moments later at a stoplight.

They said Ryan got out of the car, argued with them, then got back in his vehicle and drove away.

NFL'S BATTLE WITH DRINKING AND DRIVING CONTINUES AS KEENAN ALLEN FORMALLY CHARGED IN INDIANAPOLIS

Former NFL coach & ESPN analyst Rex Ryan of 'ESPN's Sunday's NFL Countdown' speaks onstage during the ESPN portion of the 2017 Summer Television Critics Association Press Tour at The Beverly Hilton Hotel on July 26, 2017 in Beverly Hills, California. (Frederick M. Brown/Getty Images)

Holland did not explain how he was able to catch up to Ryan's vehicle after having both his feet run over by a truck.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Ryan, 63, surrendered to authorities and was arrested on six outstanding misdemeanor charges Wednesday, a day after he allegedly struck the pedestrians, according to the Metropolitan Nashville Police Department.

The police said Ryan hit the individuals, who suffered minor injuries, as they were crossing the street. The pedestrians had a walk sign when Ryan, who was turning from 4th Avenue, ran over their feet and made contact with one of their legs, the police said in a statement.

The former New York Jets and Buffalo Bills head coach was charged with two counts of leaving the scene of an accident, two counts of failure to give information and/or render aid, and two counts of failure to obey a traffic control signal.

FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

Armando Salguero is OutKick's Senior NFL Writer.

articles.title: Fake AI event invites target Microsoft and Google logins
articles.excerpt:
Google General Counsel Halimah Delaine Prado joins 'Fox & Friends' to detail how Google is fighting AI-powered phishing scams.

An invitation to an exclusive OpenAI event lands in your inbox. It promi...
articles.body_text:
Google General Counsel Halimah Delaine Prado joins 'Fox & Friends' to detail how Google is fighting AI-powered phishing scams.

An invitation to an exclusive OpenAI event lands in your inbox. It promises a look at the latest AI tools and even offers three months of ChatGPT Pro for free. All you have to do is register using your work account. Sounds like a pretty good deal, right? Well, before you click that registration button, there's something you should know. Cybercriminals are using fake AI event invitations to trick employees into giving them access to their Microsoft and Google accounts. And some of these attacks can get past the extra security checks many of us rely on.

According to a new report from Push Security, attackers have created convincing event registration pages impersonating OpenAI, SpaceX and Anthropic. Push Security says it detected and blocked visits to the malicious event registration pages on its customers' browsers in late October 2026. The concerning part is how easily an invitation that appears legitimate can lead to someone handing over access to their work account. Here's what researchers discovered and how to protect yourself.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

FAKE CHATGPT BILLING EMAILS CAN STEAL YOUR LOGIN

Cybercriminals are impersonating OpenAI, SpaceX and Anthropic with fake AI event invitations designed to steal employees’ Microsoft and Google login credentials. (Tristan Spinski for The Washington Post via Getty Images)

The attackers are taking advantage of the growing interest in artificial intelligence. After all, plenty of employees want to learn how AI can make their jobs easier. A free premium subscription could be enough to get someone's attention. The phishing pages discovered by Push Security promote events that appear to come from recognizable technology companies. One fake OpenAI event advertised a November 4 livestream called "ChatGPT for Social & Digital Marketing Teams." The registration page promised three months of ChatGPT Pro to participants. Another page promoted an invitation-only SpaceX briefing scheduled for November 12. Visitors could supposedly choose between three months of Grok Heavy or a "SpaceX share."

Researchers also identified a phishing page impersonating an Anthropic event at AWS re 2026. That page was no longer active when they investigated it. These pages impersonated legitimate technology companies, and the advertised rewards were part of the phishing scheme. Push Security did not suggest that OpenAI, SpaceX or Anthropic operated these fraudulent events. And here's where things get especially concerning. The fake websites tell visitors they must sign in using their corporate Microsoft or Google accounts to complete registration and claim the promised rewards. That request opens the door to the phishing attack.

The criminals have put considerable effort into making these invitations appear credible. Rather than sending people directly to an obvious phishing website, they use familiar online services to help disguise where the links lead. Push Security found that the campaign routed visitors through shortened links associated with Google and Zapier. Earlier related attacks also used legitimate Zoom event pages and GoTo Webinar's email infrastructure. As a result, someone checking an invitation might see a familiar service before reaching the malicious registration page. Researchers have not confirmed the initial delivery method for every invitation in the newer campaign.

Once someone reaches the suspicious site, another familiar feature appears. A Cloudflare security challenge asks visitors to confirm they are human. You have probably encountered similar checks while shopping or visiting legitimate websites. However, criminals can use them too. In this campaign, the challenge also made it harder for automated security scanners to examine the malicious pages. After completing the check, visitors arrive at what looks like a professional event registration website. They're presented with two familiar buttons: "Continue with Microsoft" and "Continue with Google." Depending on which button someone selects, the attackers launch a different method designed to capture access to that account.

This is where the attack gets clever. If someone selects "Continue with Microsoft," the phishing website connects to a service called Kali365. It's a phishing-as-a-service platform that criminals can use to carry out account attacks. Kali365 generates a Microsoft device authentication code. The fake registration page then instructs the visitor to copy that code and enter it on Microsoft's legitimate sign-in website.

Now, here's why that can fool someone. Microsoft's device authentication process is real. You may have used something similar when connecting a streaming device to an account. However, the attacker started this authentication request. When the victim enters the supplied code and approves the sign-in, Microsoft can issue authentication tokens to the attacker's session.

Those tokens may provide access to Microsoft 365 resources without the attacker needing the account password. And the attack may continue from there. Push Security found that the campaign redirects Microsoft users to another phishing service called VoidProxy after the device code step. That second stage attempts to capture their password and authenticated session cookie. A successful compromise could expose company email or documents stored in Microsoft 365. Other connected workplace applications may also be at risk, depending on the permissions and access associated with the compromised account.

The Google option takes another approach. When visitors click "Continue with Google," the phishing page opens a pop-up that appears to contain Google's familiar sign-in screen. However, that login process runs through VoidProxy, which acts as an intermediary between the person signing in and Google's actual authentication service.

As someone enters their credentials, the phishing service can capture the information. It can also intercept certain multifactor authentication responses and steal session cookies. So, what exactly is a session cookie? Think of it as a digital pass that helps a website remember you've already signed in. Once your identity has been verified, that cookie can allow you to continue using your account without entering your password on every page.

If a criminal obtains a usable session cookie, they may be able to reuse that authenticated session and gain access without completing the usual login process again. That's why these attacks are particularly dangerous for people who believe that enabling multifactor authentication automatically protects them from every account takeover attempt. It's important to note that Push Security documented the malicious infrastructure and blocked visits to the phishing pages. Its report did not establish how many accounts, if any, were successfully compromised through this campaign.

HACKERS HIDE DANGEROUS FAKE AI DOWNLOADS BEHIND GOOGLE ADS

A convincing Google sign-in window appears over a fraudulent SpaceX event page, allowing attackers to capture login credentials and authentication sessions. (Push Security)

The attackers are combining two phishing services behind the same registration pages. Kali365 targets Microsoft's device authentication process, while VoidProxy targets authenticated login sessions. Meanwhile, the fake event websites borrow the appearance of familiar brands. The criminals can also change their websites and event themes as older pages get discovered. Researchers also discovered that the fraudulent registration pages could automatically display content in a visitor's language. That allowed the attackers to adapt the same phishing campaign for people in different regions without creating entirely new websites. Push Security identified two phishing kits used to create the fake event pages. The researchers call them ZoomMock and MSDRoot. They found evidence suggesting the same operators were responsible for both kits, although the connection was not conclusively established.

Researchers also found no evidence linking the developers of Kali365 and VoidProxy. Instead, they believe the attackers behind the event campaign are customers of both phishing services. The result is an attack that can appear credible at several points. A shortened link may use a recognized service. A security challenge can look legitimate. Even the Microsoft authentication page can be genuine. For employees who regularly attend virtual meetings or participate in industry webinars, that familiarity could make the scam harder to recognize.

In response to our request for comment, a Microsoft spokesperson said, "We take reports of malicious online activity seriously and continuously work to help protect our customers from evolving threats. Microsoft Defender includes detections to block the threats identified in the report."

We also reached out to Google, OpenAI, Anthropic and SpaceX for comment but did not receive responses before our deadline.

A few careful habits can significantly reduce your chances of falling for these attacks. Here's how to protect yourself.

If you receive an unexpected invitation from OpenAI, SpaceX or another technology company, take a moment to check whether the event actually exists. Open a new browser tab and visit the organization's official website yourself. Look for the event through its verified channels. If necessary, contact the organizer using information obtained independently of the invitation. Be especially careful when an unfamiliar event requests your corporate account credentials.

An invitation promising premium AI access may sound appealing, especially when the offer appears to come from a respected technology company. However, the promise of something valuable can encourage people to act before checking the details. If registration requires you to sign in with a work account to receive a reward, verify the offer independently before proceeding.

This is one of the most important lessons from the campaign. If a website asks you to copy a device authentication code and enter it on a Microsoft page, consider whether you initiated a legitimate device sign-in. If you were simply registering for a webinar, that unexpected device code request should raise concerns. Even a legitimate Microsoft authentication webpage can become part of a phishing attack when criminals trick you into approving their request. Pay attention to any Microsoft sign-in prompt asking you to approve access. Even if the website address is legitimate, you could be authorizing a session started by a criminal.

THE BEST DEFENSE AGAINST HIGH-TECH AI SCAMS IS LOW-TECH SKEPTICISM, EXPERT WARNS

Hackers are using fraudulent AI event registration pages promising free ChatGPT Pro subscriptions and exclusive access to trick employees into compromising their work accounts. (Felix Zahn/Photothek via Getty Images)

Before entering account credentials, examine the website address and consider how you arrived there. A page displaying familiar branding may still belong to a criminal. Shortened links can also conceal the final destination. Whenever possible, open Microsoft or Google directly through a trusted bookmark or the official website. Remember that a padlock icon and HTTPS connection do not guarantee that a website is trustworthy.

Continue using multifactor authentication, even though some phishing attacks can defeat certain forms of it. For stronger protection, consider phishing-resistant authentication, such as FIDO2 security keys or supported passkeys. These methods can help prevent attackers from stealing credentials through fraudulent login websites. While these methods offer stronger protection against phishing, they cannot guarantee protection if an attacker obtains a valid authenticated session through another method. However, no single security measure stops every possible attack. Organizations should also consider additional controls to protect authenticated sessions and reduce the risk of stolen tokens being reused. Microsoft recommends restricting device code authentication wherever it isn't necessary. IT administrators can apply those restrictions through Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policies after reviewing legitimate business needs.

Strong antivirus software and browser protections can help identify suspicious links and dangerous websites before you interact with them. Look for protection that helps detect phishing pages and malicious downloads. Keep your browser and security tools updated so they can benefit from the latest available protections. However, remember that attackers frequently create new websites to evade detection. Security software can reduce your exposure, but it cannot guarantee that every fraudulent invitation will be blocked. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android & iOS devices at Cyberguy.com

If you've already clicked on a suspicious event invitation, don't panic. What you do next depends on how far you got in the sign-in process. Here are the steps to take to protect your accounts.

The sooner you report suspicious activity, the better the chances of stopping unauthorized access before more damage occurs.

Criminals know people are eager to keep up with AI, and they're using that interest to make their scams more convincing. An invitation offering free ChatGPT Pro or access to an exclusive event sounds pretty tempting. But what really concerns me is that you can land on Microsoft's actual sign-in page and still give a hacker access to your account. Think about that. Even checking the website address may not be enough to protect you. So before you sign up for that next AI event, take a minute to make sure it's legitimate. I'd rather miss out on a free offer than hand a criminal access to my work account.
